messages.subject: Aw: Re: How to use CPO?
messages.subject_clean: Aw: Re: How to use CPO?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

we use the logarithmic score calculated as -mean(log(inla.result$cpo)). However, you should also have a look at inla.result$failure to see whether all CPO values are reliable (see the FAQ section for details). According to a paper by Stone (1977), the cross-validated mean logarithmic score is asymptotically equivalent to the AIC, if the observations are independent. We used the logarithmic score  for disease mapping models including spatial effects, see for example Schrödle et al 2010 <http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1467-9876.2010.00740.x/abstract>. I think DIC and the logarithmic score need not to give exactly the same results. For  example, If you have many random effects in your model, DIC tends to underpenalize complex models, see Plummer, Biostatistics, 2008.

Best regards,

Andrea

messages.body_plain:
you're right.

inla has an issue when the 'arg', in 'f(arg,....)' is not numeric, then
these values are converted to numerical values and the actual
non-numeric values of 'arg' is lost.   in your case there was a
'as.numeric()' that was missing. I have rebuildt the package, so if you
do inla.upgrade(testing=T), you're done.

the issue about the labels is on the TODO list, as if

i = factor(c("a","b"))

and

formula = y ~ f(i,....)

one would expect that you could find the marginal for level "a"
somewhere, but you cannot, as these are converted to numerics

> as.numeric(factor(c("a","b")))

so "a" is "1".

this wasn't done correct from the beginning in the implementation, and
its messy.

I'll see what I can do.

H

> Re: [r-inla] NaN in DIC

> Thu, 22 Sep 2011 11:27:37 -0400

> Facundo Muñoz <fam...@gmail.com>
>                              Para:
> Håvard Rue <hr...@math.ntnu.no>
>
>
> Hi Havard,
>
> Let me ask a couple of questions on this problem:
>
> 1. The example you added in the FAQ does not get NaN in DIC.
> How can we 'detect' that there is a problem, then?
> Only by looking at the posterior precision for the iid term?

there is unfortunately no sign that this particular problem that you
refer to,

http://www.r-inla.org/faq#TOC-INLA-seems-to-work-great-for-near-a

fails.  sorry about that.

> 2. In my dataset, the simple model Y ~ 1 + f(spatial, model=spde) still
> gets NaN in DIC.
> Although now there is borrowing of strength.
> Might it be suffering from the same problem, yet?
> I looked at the hyperparameters but seem to be well identified, although
> K.0 gets negative values. Is this ok? Actually I don't know what T.0 and
> K.0 are.

you shouldn't really. can you send me the data and R so I can rerun it
here?

as you say, it might suffereing from the same problem, as NaN comes from
overflow in the numerics.

K.0 defines the \kappa^2 parameter as \log\kappa^2 = K.0, while \log
\prec=\T.0, in the SPDE.

There is a new interface to the SPDE stuff coming up (Finn is working on
it), which is called spde2, where the parametersiation will be much more
transparent and more general.

Best
H
